extracted.intended_audience: inventors, in-house counsel, patent practitioners, and companies considering USPTO Track One prioritized examination
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for filing and using the USPTO Track One Prioritized Examination program for utility and plant patent applications, including eligibility, procedural requirements, timelines, fees, and strategic considerations for when to elect expedited examination.

rubrics_metrics.name: When a Track One Request Can Be Filed
rubrics_metrics.description: A request may only accompany a newly filed U.S. nonprovisional application, or a Request for Continued Examination (RCE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track One cannot be requested for U.S. national phase (371) filings or design applications. Time the request to either accompany initial filing or a valid RCE.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligible Application Types
rubrics_metrics.description: Track One is available for utility patent applications and plant patent applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude design applications and national phase (371) entries—those are ineligible for the program.

rubrics_metrics.name: Claim Limitations at Filing
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must meet limits at filing: no more than 4 independent claims, no more than 30 total claims, and no multiple dependent claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amendments may be filed at the time of the request to ensure compliance with these limits; ensure claim count and dependency structure are in compliance before requesting Track One.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Filings (ADS or Declaration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each application must include either an Application Data Sheet (ADS) or a signed inventor declaration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants often satisfy this requirement by filing an ADS with the application; do not omit these formalities or the request may be denied or delayed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Annual Quota and Program Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO accepts a limited number of Track One requests each fiscal year; as of July 8, 2025, the cap is 20,000 requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Historically the cap has not been reached, so availability is rarely a concern, but applicants should monitor the annual quota and USPTO announcements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Acceptance Timing and Formalities
rubrics_metrics.description: When formalities are met, Track One requests are typically accepted within about two months.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure all formal requirements are met on filing to avoid delays; prompt acceptance facilitates rapid examiner assignment and expedited prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: First Office Action Timing Under Track One
rubrics_metrics.description: After acceptance an Examiner is assigned quickly and a first Office Action often issues within about one month; applicants should expect their first substantive communication 2–3 months after filing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early issuance of a first office action allows earlier assessment of patentability; be prepared to engage with the Examiner and respond quickly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Prosecution Timeline Objective
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO’s objective is to issue a final disposition (allowance or final rejection) within 12 months of acceptance into Track One.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Many applications conclude sooner if applicants respond promptly and use examiner interviews; plan prosecution workflow to hit short deadlines to realize the 12‑month objective.

rubrics_metrics.name: No Extensions Constraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Requesting an extension of time automatically removes the application from Track One.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must be prepared to meet all deadlines on schedule; requesting extensions is an anti-pattern if preserving prioritized status is important.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fees for Prioritized Examination
rubrics_metrics.description: Current USPTO fees for prioritized examination: Small entity $1,806; Large entity $4,515.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These fees are in addition to standard filing, examination, and search fees (or RCE fees if Track One is filed with an RCE). Factor the fee into cost/benefit decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Strategic Benefits of Track One
rubrics_metrics.description: Track One supports early protection for product/method launches, earlier clarity on patentability, strengthened licensing/partnership positions, and streamlined examiner engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use Track One when early issuance materially benefits commercialization, fundraising, licensing, or regulatory interactions; consider interviewing examiners early to accelerate prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: When Track One Is the Right Choice
rubrics_metrics.description: Track One is particularly useful when applicants need early patent issuance for commercial milestones, have a defined embodiment requiring quick protection, expect near‑term licensing/diligence/fundraising, or plan continuation filings for broader claims.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Industries commonly using Track One include biotech, pharma, medical devices, polymer science, engineering, and software. Align Track One use with product timelines and portfolio strategy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portfolio and Continuation Strategy Considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider how Track One fits within a broader portfolio strategy, especially if pursuing continuation filings or parallel applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Because Track One prosecution is fast and claim expansion during Track One is impractical, applicants often secure narrow protection early and pursue broader claim scopes in continuations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Practical Readiness Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Because examination proceeds quickly, applicants should be prepared to respond on time to Office Actions and engage quickly with the Examiner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure claims are well‑defined at filing; have counsel and prosecution resources ready; failing to respond promptly risks losing the benefits of Track One (and removal from the program if extensions are sought).

rubrics_metrics.name: Use with RCE Filings
rubrics_metrics.description: A Track One request may accompany a Request for Continued Examination (RCE).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When filed with an RCE, Track One can expedite continued prosecution, but applicants must still meet the claim/filing/formality limits and pay the prioritized fee in addition to RCE fees.
